previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with a history of common variable immunodeficiency, diffuse large B-cell lymphoma status post allogeneic stem cell transplant, and a colostomy presented with significant bleeding from her ostomy site, lasting several hours and causing fatigue and lightheadedness. Evaluation revealed the bleed originated at the skin-stoma junction, likely due to irritation and low platelets. She was treated with Surgicel and two units of platelets, which stopped the bleeding. Her diarrhea, which had been malodorous and watery, resolved during admission, and stool testing was negative for C. difficile and other pathogens. Tacrolimus dose was increased due to a subtherapeutic level. She remained stable, with no recurrence of bleeding or infection, and was discharged home with follow-up plans, a walker for gait instability, and instructions to avoid manipulating the stoma.

somnolence. An infectious workup was performed, and urine and

 Mucosal thickening of the right frontal and ethmoid air cells has  increased.

paritally visualized on today's exam, and closely followed on MRI. Asymmetric

EXAMINATION:  MR HEAD W AND W/O CONTRAST

INDICATION:  Evaluate for intracranial pathology in a patient with a history
of CVID and recurrent diffuse large B-cell lymphoma with CNS involvement, now
presenting with somnolence and gait disturbance.

TECHNIQUE:  Sagittal and axial T1 weighted imaging were performed. After
administration of 6 mL of Gadavist intravenous contrast, axial imaging was
performed with gradient echo, FLAIR, diffusion, and T1 technique. Sagittal
MPRAGE imaging was performed and re-formatted in axial and coronal
orientations.

FINDINGS: 

The patient is status post left parietal craniotomy and resection of a

again likely related to chronic small vessel ischemic disease.  There is no
